articles.title: Jennifer Lopez Teases ‘Monster-in-Law’ Sequel With Jane Fonda: ‘We’re Talking About Maybe Doing Another One’
articles.summary: Jennifer Lopez and Jane Fonda might reunite for a “Monster-in-Law” follow-up, the singer and actress teased recently. In a clip from Lopez’s upcoming appearance on “The Drew Barrymore Show,” she reminisced with the host about past projects, including the 2005 rom-com she starred in with Fonda.
body: The rom-com starred Fonda as Viola Fields, a mother-in-law-to-be determined to stop her son (Vartan) from marrying Charlotte “Charlie” Cantilini (Lopez). Monet Mazur, Wanda Sykes, Adam Scott, Annie Parisse and Will Arnett also starred.
Lopez said working with Fonda was “amazing.” “I mean, loved her.” She added, “We’re talking about maybe doing another one.”
Lopez and Fonda have remained close since filming “Monster-in-Law.” In 2013, Fonda spoke at Lopez’s Hollywood Walk of Fame ceremony, and the two reunited at a 2025 pre-Oscars party.
Barrymore also showed the audience shots from Lopez’s Fonda-inspired Halloween costume from this year. “The Halloween Barbarella nod was as hot as it gets,” Barrymore said.

articles.title: Kieran Culkin Says a ‘Succession’ Spinoff ‘Would Be a Terrible Idea’: ‘What Are You Hoping For? “Cousin Greg: The Sitcom?”‘
articles.summary: Sorry, “Succession” fans — Kieran Culkin is shutting down any possibility of a spinoff once and for all. The actor, currently starring in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping” as a young Caesar Flickerman, joined the “Heart Breakfast” radio show on Friday to discuss the new film, though hosts…
body: “I know we’re not here to talk about this, but I’m still grieving the end of ‘Succession,’” said Holden, to which Culkin responded: “Oh, you are? Get over it. It’s been three years!” When asked about a potential for a spinoff, Culkin answered, “Of course not. I think that would be a terrible idea… I mean, what are you hoping for? ‘Cousin Greg: The Sitcom?’… Yeah, that would be a terrible idea.”
And though the “A Real Pain” actor is steadfast about not retreading the show’s familiar territory, he noted that he misses playing Roman Roy and the “whole thing.”

Culkin continued: “It was fun. It was one of those where Jesse Armstrong, the showrunner, spent the entire last season trying to figure out if there was a way to do one more. I never wanted to know what was going to happen in the season and on the fourth one I did ask and when he pitched me the end of the season and I went ‘well, that kind of sounds like it’s the end of the show.’ But when he pitched me three different ideas of what season 5 could be, they all sounded good… But it ended perfectly. The way it was supposed to.

articles.title: Mahershala Ali Says It ‘Doesn’t Matter’ That He’s Won 2 Oscars Because ‘There Are Not Roles for Me’ in ‘the Vast Majority of Projects’: ‘You’re Like Everybody Else Waiting’
articles.summary: Mahershala Ali got candid about the impact — or lack thereof — his two Oscar wins have had on his career in Hollywood while appearing on a recent episode of Carmelo Anthony and Kazeem “Kaz” Famuyide’s “7PM in Brooklyn” podcast.
body: He continued: “The vast majority of projects that get greenlit, there are not roles for me in those. You gotta think that way, you know what I mean? So, it doesn’t matter if I got 17 Oscars. If someone is not writing something for you or greenlighting something with you in mind, you’re like everybody else waiting and looking and searching.”

While the star noted that actors could produce their own projects, the timeline is usually as least a “three to five year” journey. When asked by Famuyide if an Oscar win validates Black actors, Ali responded: “It’s kind of just talk. It doesn’t translate to anything real. You don’t want to find yourself in a situation where, oh, that’s ‘the diversity project.’ You just want to do great material as a Black person. You’re not thinking of yourself as this exotic other, per se. You just are living your life.”

Most recently, Ali starred in Bassam Tariq’s “ Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother,” which hit theaters on Sept. 25. Tariq was also the original director of Marvel’s failed “Blade” movie, in which Ali was set to star in the title role, which he recently discussed in an interview with The New Arab.

articles.title: Seth Rogen Says Brad Pitt and ‘12 Years a Slave’ Cast Would Visit ‘This Is the End’ Set to ‘Perk Up’ Because They Were ‘in a Bummed-Out Headspace’ While Filming
articles.summary: Seth Rogen and Brad Pitt spent time together while shooting very different films in 2013. Rogen recalled Pitt, Michael Fassbender, Chiwetel Ejiofor and other cast members from “12 Years a Slave” spending time on the set of his comedy “This Is the End” while the two films were both shooting in New…
body: “Actually, what’s so weird is I had met him — we made ‘This Is the End’ at the same time they made ’12 Years a Slave’ in New Orleans together,” Rogen told podcast host Josh Horowitz. “Understandably, the cast and crew of ’12 Years a Slave’ were in a bummed-out headspace a lot of the time.”

“12 Years a Slave” starred Ejiofor as a free Black man named Solomon Northup who was kidnapped in 1841 and sold into slavery in Louisiana. Fassbender played plantation owner Edwin Epps and Pitt played an abolitionist named Samuel Bass who helped Northup regain his freedom.

Meanwhile, Rogen was shooting “This Is the End” with Jay Baruchel, James Franco, Jonah Hill, Craig Robinson, Danny McBride and a host of other celebrities. The actors played dramatized versions of themselves in a bizarre apocalyptic scene at a Hollywood house party.

articles.title: Spitting Image co-creator Peter Fluck dies aged 85
articles.summary: The 85-year-old he died in the early hours of Saturday at home in Cornwall, following a recent illness.
body: Peter Fluck, co-creator of award-winning satirical puppet show Spitting Image, has died aged 85.

Spitting Image was immensely popular and sometimes controversial, running from 1984-1996 across 18 seasons, and featured puppet caricatures of celebrities, politicians and royals, including former Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher and Queen Elizabeth the Queen Mother.
"The spirit that Spitting Image brought to the country was epoch defining," a family statement said.
"With Roger Law ('Luck and Flaw'), he brought a unique cutting edge to caricaturing that later evolved into a production company that created the TV series Spitting Image," it added.

articles.title: ‘I’m opening the cage of a monster’: Taxi Driver scriptwriter Paul Schrader on unleashing AI at 80
articles.summary: Director and Scorsese collaborator is using AI in films and sees its takeover as inevitable, not just in cinema. Paul Schrader was sipping white wine in a Greenwich Village trattoria when he said how he felt about using AI to make films: “I am opening the cage of a monster and I don’t have a…
body: The 80-year-old film-maker behind Taxi Driver, Raging Bull and American Gigolo, is embracing the technology as he enters the final act of a prolific career in which he has collaborated with Martin Scorsese, Robert De Niro, Sigourney Weaver and Richard Gere.

Defying orthodox resistance among the Hollywood guilds to using AI to create synthetic actors, special effects and even scripts, Schrader is doing all of those things. It is part of what he sees as AI’s inevitable takeover, not just of cinema, the art he has pursued for half a century, writing and directing dozens of films to international acclaim, but of humankind more broadly.

“I don’t see, quite frankly, a place for Homo sapiens in the larger scheme of things,” he told the Guardian. “I don’t think there’s a story where we come out on top. In order to create a story where … man defeats the threat of AI – it’s just a bogus story.”

Yet, while directors ranging from his 1970s collaborator Steven Spielberg to the Odyssey’s Christopher Nolan, express deep scepticism about AI, Schrader is running towards, not away from, what he describes as a monster that he fears may soon imprison him.

articles.title: ‘Shakespearean tale of ego, greed and ambition’: the scandalous story of televangelism
articles.summary: Netflix documentary Primetime Preacher$ travels back to a time when evangelism found a dominant place on US television – and the shocking tabloid stories that followed.
body: For three decades, film-maker Joe Berlinger has gripped true-crime buffs with his deep dives into small-town murders and infamous serial killers. His Netflix explorations of John Wayne Gacy and Jeffrey Dahmer helped flip documentary storytelling from viewer homework to a welcome distraction.

After dedicating so much time to the life of Jeffrey Epstein, the kidnapping of JonBenét Ramsey and other unsolved mysteries, Berlinger thought Primetime Preacher$, his new Netflix documentary on America’s televangelist boom, would offer a break. But it turns out that’s a pretty juicy crime story too, about the religious right’s bank job on American politics. “The deeper resonance for me came when I realized that the global televangelism rise actually mirrors the rise of the religious right,” he says. “Religion and politics, from Reagan on, has really changed politics for the worse in my opinion. This was the birth of that.”

articles.title: Russell Brand Selling “Free Russell” Merch Via His Wellness Business While in Prison
articles.summary: He is also receiving backlash for sharing a message from behind bars, delivered by his wife, Laura Brand, on his YouTube channel on Nov. 15 where he claimed he was innocent.
body: Russell Brand is selling merchandise calling for his freedom while he’s behind bars after being sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault.

“So Russell has asked me to read something to you today,” the actor’s wife said at the start of the video, before looking to a notebook to read her husband’s message. “Beloved brothers and sisters in Christ, God bless you for your support. As you know, I am not guilty for the offenses I have been jailed for, so something strange is happening.”

Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of rape and sexual assault. The trial lasted four weeks at Southwark Crown Court, with the jury finding him guilty on one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault (he was found not guilty on two other rape charges and not guilty of attempted indecent assault).

The actor has three items featuring “Free Russell” available for purchase on the website for Reborn, his wellness business. Every item is available for $34.99; a shirt with the words “Free Russell Brand “; a hat with the same text; and another shirt that reads “Free Russell” with an image of himself.

articles.title: Luca Guadagnino Says His ‘American Psycho’ Movie Not Moving Forward
articles.summary: Scott Z. Burns penned a script for Lionsgate's new take on the Bret Easton Ellis novel, which was previously adapted into a 2000 film starring Christian Bale as Patrick Bateman.
body: Luca Guadagnino ‘s adaptation of American Psycho is no longer moving forward.
While appearing on Deadline ‘s Crew Call podcast with Anthony D’Alessandro, Guadagnino confirmed that his new adaptation of Bret Easton Ellis’ bestselling novel is no longer happening.
“Scott Z. Burns wrote a fantastic script. Unfortunately for me, as we speak, it’s not happening,” Guadagnino said.
The project was first announced in October 2024, with Frenesy Films producing. At the time, it was described as a new interpretation of Ellis’ novel rather than a remake of the original film.

articles.title: Why Beetee Latier From The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Looks So Familiar
articles.summary: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping stars Kelvin Harrison Jr. as the younger version of Beetee Latier. Here's where you might know Harrison from.
body: This article contains spoilers for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping."

Prequel film "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" reveals the details of how Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada, Woody Harrelson in the original films) won the 50th Hunger Games... and lost everything else in his life, turning him into a miserable man using alcohol to cope. Yet "The Hunger Games: Catching Fire" revealed Haymitch wasn't merely the burnout he first appeared to be, but a key member of the rebellion against the Capitol.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" shows the beginning of that, particularly Haymitch's early alliance with Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons, filling in for the late Philip Seymour Hoffman). Younger versions of several past Hunger Games victors first introduced in "Catching Fire" also show up in "Sunrise on the Reaping," including the tech wizard Beetee Latier (Kelvin Harrison Jr. doing an uncanny vocal impression of original Beetee actor Jeffrey Wright).
points: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping stars Kelvin Harrison Jr. as the younger version of Beetee Latier.

articles.title: Guy Pearce's Remake Of A '60s Sci-Fi Classic Deserved Better At The Box Office
articles.summary: In 2002, Guy Pearce starred in an ill-fated movie adaptation of a classic sci-fi novel that had already been adapted into a film in the 1960s.
body: Simon Wells' 2002 sci-fi flick "The Time Machine" was extrapolated from H.G. Wells' celebrated 1895 novel, one of the best sci-fi novels ever written, and also from George Pal's famed 1960 adaptation of the same story, itself one of the best time travel movies of all time. Made for a budget of $80 million, "The Time Machine" didn't overwhelm at the box office, earning almost $124 million worldwide. Critics were very unkind to "The Time Machine," and the film only has a 28% approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes, based on 151 reviews.

The movie isn't great, reducing the intellectualism of Wells' original novel into a rote sci-fi action thriller, but there was a steampunk quirkiness to "The Time Machine" that could have been more openly embraced. It was even nominated for an Oscar for Best Makeup.
